title: NWIS Feature Record
description: Version 0.1.0 feature record schema. Each record contains derived features computed from one NWIS canonical telemetry record plus its time-windowed context. Features are computed only from data at or before the record timestamp (no look-ahead). Units are unverified unless explicitly stated.

feature_version.description: Feature engineering version. Bump when feature definitions change.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp. Inherited from canonical record.

well_id.description: NWIS internal well identifier. Preserved from canonical record.

source_row_index.description: Row index from original source. Preserved for full traceability.

data_origin.description: Provenance class. Preserved from canonical record.

telemetry_status.description: Record-level telemetry status. Preserved from canonical record.

quality_features.description: Data quality and telemetry health features.

signal_features.description: Per-channel signal features: current value, rolling statistics, deltas.

state_features.description: Observable signal state indicators. NOT physical-event labels.

relationship_features.description: Cross-channel relationship features. Statistical associations only. Not causal claims.

NullableNumber.description: A numeric feature value that may be null if the input was missing or insufficient data existed for computation. NaN must not be used — use null.

_window_definitions.rationale: Windows are defined in seconds (not row counts) because the WELL-1 dataset has variable sampling intervals (median ~4.9s) and contains a ~29,493-second telemetry gap. Row-count windows would erroneously span across sparse intervals. min_periods=1 is used to avoid discarding early rows, but features computed from very few observations are labelled with a coverage note.
_window_definitions.gap_threshold_rationale: A time delta of >300 seconds between consecutive records is treated as an abnormal interval. This threshold is 5x the dataset's p99 inter-sample interval. It is a heuristic and not a physical definition of a gap.
